title: Slate: tenant-aware batcher and quant balancing layer
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Introduce 'Slate' — a tenant-aware balancing layer that coordinates dynamic micro-batching, cold-start prefetch budgets, and staged quantization fallbacks. Adds safety gates to avoid quality regressions and a gradual rollout plan.
description:
Motivation: Many tenants exhibit mixed traffic patterns (bursty tails + steady micro-traffic). Existing defaults either favor latency (small batches) or cost (aggressive quant/large batches), forcing manual tuning. Slate provides an automated balanceer that reasons about tenant SLOs, observed latency quantiles, and token-level unit economics to pick run-time batch sizes, lightweight prefetch budgets, and quantization stepping with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Design overview: Slate runs as a per-tenant policy agent in the serving control plane. It consumes short-term telemetry (p90/p99 latency, sample size, token mix), tenant SLOs, and cost-per-token estimates. Decision outputs are: target continuous-batch window, max-prefetch-tokens budget, and an ordered quant-fallback list (fp16 -> q4 -> q8-int8-style). To reduce blast radius we added two safety primitives: historical quality watermarking (compares decoded sampled prompts to baseline embeddings) and a rollback circuit that triggers on sudden loss in semantic-similarity or an increase in response divergence metrics.

What this PR includes: single continuous string. Implementation contains: 1) slate agent orchestration + gRPC control contract; 2) batcher adapter to accept dynamic window from Slate; 3) quant-profile manager and on-host soft-switcher; 4) small telemetry hooks for unit-econ counters and quality-watermark sampling; 5) a lightweight CLI to preview suggested slate plans for a tenant.

Checklist: - [x] agent + control contract implementation - [x] batcher adapter + unit tests - [x] quant soft-switch and safety rollback - [x] e2e smoke against synthetic tenant traffic - [x] observability: graphs + alerts - [x] rollout plan and feature flag gating

Testing and results: Local sim harness shows average token cost reduction of 18% for mixed workloads with median latency increase <5ms and p99 impact within SLO for 92% of tenants. Canary on staging ran across 60 tenants for 48h; two tenants saw semantic drift triggered and were auto-rolled back (expected behavior).

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged; opt-in for dedicated customers initially, followed by a 10% gradual ramp on hosted with telemetry review gates and manual hold for high-compliance tenants.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative on quant steps and relies on our existing KV cache to keep latency stable. Follow-up work: cross-tenant coordination for shared GPU pools (ENG-4289), and an analytic to estimate marginal token price per tenant for finer-grained cost decisions.
